instructions:
Each item is an ontology term that a column of sample metadata in a gene
expression study can mean. Write up to 5 aliases for each term: other ways a
researcher would write that same variable as a column header in sample
metadata.

Good aliases:
- common abbreviations and acronyms ("sbp" for systolic blood pressure)
- shorter everyday phrasings ("systolic bp", "visual acuity")
- the plain name of the quantity when the term's label is wordy
  ("intraocular pressure" for "intraocular pressure measurement")

Rules:
- An alias must mean the same variable as the term: not a broader or narrower
  one, and not a related one.
- No values ("male", "high"), units on their own, gene or tool names, or
  dataset-specific codes.
- No alias that only rewords the label trivially (plural, case,
  punctuation). Those are matched already.
- Fewer is better than wrong. If a term has no natural alias, return an empty
  list.

Examples:
- systolic blood pressure -> ["sbp", "systolic bp", "systolic pressure"]
- intraocular pressure measurement -> ["intraocular pressure", "iop"]
- visual acuity measurement -> ["visual acuity", "va"]

items.label: vascular endothelial function measurement

items.label: photoreceptor cell layer thickness measurement
items.definition: A measure of the thickness of photoreceptor cell receptor (PCR) segments of the retina. It can be non-invasively measured using optical coherence tomography (OCT).

items.label: hemorheological measurement
items.definition: A measurement of the flow characteristics of blood and its elements. Hemorheology indicators include whole blood viscosity, plasma viscosity, erythrocyte aggregation, erythrocyte rigidity, erythrocyte deformation, fibrinogen, and hematocrit.

items.label: erythrocyte aggregation
items.definition: A measurement of the reversible formation of clumps of red blood cells under low-shear conditions or stasis.

items.label: erythrocyte deformability
items.definition: A measurement of the ability of erythrocytes to change shape without rupturing, as they pass through narrow spaces, such as the microvasculature.

items.label: visual masking measurement
